morningSummary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 — Midday News. Updated at 12:00 Europe/Paris. Presented by Sophie Laurent.

GLOBAL LEAD — APEC diplomacy has accelerated in Shenzhen. Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin have held talks, and Donald Trump has arrived in China and been welcomed by Xi. A trilateral meeting is expected Thursday; it has not yet taken place. Meanwhile, the Quad leaders are meeting in Manila, with critical minerals, AI and maritime security on the agenda.

NIGERIA — The APC and opposition parties are trading accusations over protests and political violence. The Senate has called for an investigation into reported attacks involving Tinubu, Obi and Atiku. Separately, the NDC is demanding a forensic audit of an alleged ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL pipeline-security-related receivables figure. This is a party allegation and interpretation of financial disclosures, not proof of a single payment or wrongdoing.

MIDDLE EAST — Iran has expanded attacks across the Gulf, with reported targeting of a US base in Kuwait and further attacks toward Bahrain. The Strait of Hormuz and commercial shipping remain exposed to heightened risk.

EUROPE — France's public-sector pay dispute continues. The UK has imposed sanctions on eight Israeli firms linked to West Bank settlements and on a group accused of obstructing aid to Gaza. A train collision near Prague injured 46 people; investigators are examining the cause.

AFRICA — Senegal has qualified for AFCON 2027 after Mozambique defeated Ethiopia. Sudan-Ethiopia tensions continue amid unverified mutual allegations, while Mozambique opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane faces trial over charges he denies.

ASIA AND THE AMERICAS — Canada is seeking wider Asia-Pacific trade and energy links. The International Court of Justice is expected to issue its Myanmar Rohingya Genocide Convention ruling on Thursday. Japan's energy import exposure remains a concern as Gulf tensions persist.

GLOBAL PICTURE — Trade diplomacy, energy security, electoral accountability and international law are driving today's headlines. RadiantWaves separates verified events from political allegations and official claims.

topStories.title: APC accuses ADC and NDC of fuelling protests; opposition demands evidence
topStories.summary: The APC campaign council has accused opposition parties of sponsoring protests and political disruption. The ADC and NDC reject the claims and say public anger over hardship is genuine. No independent finding proving the allegation has been reported.
topStories.content: The exchange has sharpened political tensions ahead of the 2027 elections. The APC Presidential Campaign Council alleges that opposition parties are organising protests and recruiting young people to disrupt political activities. The ADC and NDC deny the accusations and argue that citizens have legitimate reasons to protest over economic hardship and governance. The public should distinguish political claims from verified findings: no independent investigation or court ruling has established that either party organised violence. Political leaders should condemn attacks regardless of affiliation, while security agencies should investigate impartially and publish evidence where lawful.

topStories.title: NDC demands forensic audit of alleged ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security costs
topStories.summary: The Nigeria Democratic Congress is questioning an ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL receivables figure linked to pipeline and energy security, demanding disclosure and a forensic audit. The figure and its interpretation require examination of audited accounts and government explanations.
topStories.content: The NDC has challenged the Tinubu administration over what it describes as an opaque ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security bill or receivables balance associated with NNPCL. The party says the amount is larger than the 2025 defence and security allocation and is demanding a forensic audit, disclosure of contractors and an account of services delivered. This is an opposition party's interpretation of the company's financial disclosures, not proof that ₦11.2 trillion was paid out as a single contract or that funds were misappropriated. The government and NNPCL should publish a clear reconciliation of the accounting entries, contractual obligations, payments, beneficiaries and security outcomes.

topStories.whyItMatters: Transparent accounting of oil revenue and security expenditure is central to public trust, especially while communities face insecurity.
topStories.whatHappensNext: The key test is whether NNPCL and the government publish a detailed, independently auditable explanation and respond to the party's claims.

topStories.title: Senate calls for investigation into reported attacks involving Tinubu, Obi and Atiku
topStories.summary: The Senate has called for an investigation into reported attacks involving political leaders and warned that candidates found responsible for electoral violence could face sanctions. The motion is not a finding of guilt against any politician.
topStories.content: The Senate's intervention follows reports of attacks and disruption involving political convoys and campaign activities. Lawmakers have urged investigations and warned that the Electoral Act provides consequences for electoral violence. The inquiry must establish the facts of each incident and identify individual responsibility; it should not be used to prejudge any party or candidate. Candidates, supporters and journalists must be able to participate in political life without intimidation.

topStories.summary: Iran widened its attacks across the Gulf on Wednesday, targeting a US air base in Kuwait and launching repeated attacks toward Bahrain. Kuwait and Bahrain said their air defences intercepted threats; no immediate casualties or damage were reported.
topStories.content: The Associated Press reports that Iran expanded attacks across the Gulf, targeting the US Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and launching further attacks toward Bahrain. Kuwait said its air defences intercepted drones, while Bahrain reported interceptions. The exchanges follow US strikes on Iranian military sites and a naval blockade that is pressuring Iran's economy and oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. AP also reported an attack on an ADNOC tanker in the strait on Tuesday, with one crew member missing and 11 injured. Military claims and damage assessments should be attributed carefully. The widening geography of attacks increases the risk to commercial shipping and regional infrastructure.

topStories.title: UK sanctions eight Israeli firms linked to West Bank settlements and aid-blocking group
topStories.summary: The UK has imposed asset freezes on eight Israeli construction and property firms involved in West Bank settlement expansion, and on the activist group Tzav 9, which Britain says has blocked aid convoys to Gaza.
topStories.content: The British government announced asset freezes targeting eight construction and property development firms it says are involved in illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist group accused of obstructing humanitarian aid entering Gaza. The measures form part of a wider UK policy response to settlement expansion and restrictions on humanitarian access. Sanctions are a government action, not a criminal conviction of every individual associated with the organisations. The measures are likely to add diplomatic pressure on Israel while raising questions about enforcement and the delivery of humanitarian assistance.

topStories.title: France strike: unions maintain pressure over wages as budget talks continue
topStories.summary: Public-sector workers have staged nationwide demonstrations over pay and purchasing power. Unions remain dissatisfied with the government's refusal to grant a general pay rise for a fourth consecutive year.
topStories.content: France's public-sector strike reflects a wider dispute over wages, purchasing power and the government's 2027 budget. Unions say public employees have lost real income since 2017 and want general pay increases. The government has announced additional index points for the lowest-paid public workers and an earlier minimum-wage increase, but has ruled out a general rise, citing public finances. The demonstrations have been largely peaceful, although reports include isolated violence and allegations of disproportionate policing. Crowd estimates differ between authorities and unions, so figures should always be attributed.

topStories.whyItMatters: The dispute affects public services, household income and the government's ability to pass its budget.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for further union action, negotiations and parliamentary budget developments.

topStories.title: Canada seeks greater trade independence through Asia-Pacific diversification
topStories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada is seeking greater economic sovereignty by diversifying trade and expanding Asian energy exports. At APEC, he highlighted tariff relief with China and deeper financial cooperation.
topStories.content: At the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is pursuing trade diversification to reduce overdependence on any single market or payment channel. He highlighted tariff relief with China, expanded access for financial firms and plans to increase liquefied natural gas exports to Asia. The approach reflects Canada's effort to widen commercial options while maintaining its security relationship with the United States. The long-term effect will depend on implementation, market access and the response from Washington and domestic industries.

topStories.title: Two trains collide near Prague; 46 people injured
topStories.summary: A collision near Prague's main railway station injured 46 people, including four with life-threatening injuries. Passengers were evacuated and investigators are examining the cause.
topStories.content: Czech emergency services said two trains collided near Prague's main railway station on Tuesday. Forty-six people were injured, four with life-threatening injuries; others suffered moderate or minor injuries. All passengers were evacuated and taken for medical care. Rail services were suspended while investigators examined the circumstances. Authorities have not yet established the cause, so speculation about driver error or equipment failure should be avoided until the inquiry reports its findings.
topStories.imageNote: Contextual image for this report; not represented as a photograph of the specific event unless stated.
topStories.whyItMatters: The incident highlights passenger safety and the need for transparent investigation of railway operations.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for the Railway Inspectorate's findings and updates on the injured and service restoration.

topStories.title: Myanmar Rohingya case: ICJ ruling expected Thursday in landmark genocide proceedings
topStories.summary: The International Court of Justice is expected to issue a substantive ruling on Thursday in The Gambia's case alleging Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention during the 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya.
topStories.content: The International Court of Justice is preparing a major decision in a case brought by The Gambia concerning Myanmar's 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya. The ruling is expected on 19 November and may clarify how states' obligations under the Genocide Convention are assessed. It will not, by itself, resolve the Rohingya humanitarian crisis or automatically deliver individual criminal accountability. Its legal reasoning could nevertheless influence future cases and the international response to mass atrocities.

topStories.whyItMatters: The case tests the international legal framework for preventing and addressing genocide.

topStories.title: AFCON 2027 qualifying: Senegal book place after Mozambique victory
topStories.summary: Senegal secured qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Mozambique defeated Ethiopia 1–0. Angola also moved top of Group B after beating South Sudan.
topStories.content: The latest AFCON 2027 qualifying results have reshaped the group picture. The Confederation of African Football confirmed that Senegal qualified after Mozambique's 1–0 win over Ethiopia on Tuesday, while Angola's 1–0 victory over South Sudan put them in control of Group B. Several East African sides, including Uganda, Tanzania and Burundi, also remain in contention after their latest results. topStories.title: Sudan-Ethiopia dispute raises fears of wider instability in the Horn of Africa
topStories.summary: Relations between Sudan and Ethiopia remain strained by competing accusations over support for armed groups. Both governments deny the allegations and independent verification remains limited.
topStories.content: The diplomatic dispute comes as Sudan's war continues and tensions persist in Ethiopia's Tigray region. Sudan has accused Ethiopia of allowing support for the Rapid Support Forces, while Ethiopia alleges Sudan backs Tigrayan rebels. Both governments deny the claims, and the allegations have not been independently established. Ethiopia has taken diplomatic measures against Sudanese consular staff. The African Union and regional partners face pressure to prevent accusations and border tensions from widening into direct confrontation.

topStories.whyItMatters: Escalation could compound displacement, food insecurity and conflict across an already fragile region.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Monitor official diplomatic steps, border developments and independent reporting from the affected areas.

topStories.title: Mozambique opposition leader Mondlane faces trial over post-election protests
topStories.summary: Opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane has appeared before the Supreme Court on charges linked to demonstrations after the disputed 2024 election. He denies wrongdoing.
topStories.content: The trial concerns charges including instigating terrorism and inciting public disorder after Mondlane rejected the 2024 election result and called for demonstrations and work boycotts. He says he was demanding electoral accountability. The case follows months of protests and allegations of excessive force by security agencies. Authorities deny that the prosecution is politically directed. The court proceedings will be watched for due process, the evidence presented and the independence of the judiciary.

topStories.whyItMatters: The case is a test of political pluralism, judicial independence and accountability after disputed elections.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Follow the court hearings, defence response and any independent human-rights monitoring.

electionWatch.title: APC accuses ADC and NDC of fuelling protests; opposition demands evidence
electionWatch.summary: The APC campaign council has accused opposition parties of sponsoring protests and political disruption. The ADC and NDC reject the claims and say public anger over hardship is genuine. No independent finding proving the allegation has been reported.
electionWatch.content: The exchange has sharpened political tensions ahead of the 2027 elections. The APC Presidential Campaign Council alleges that opposition parties are organising protests and recruiting young people to disrupt political activities. The ADC and NDC deny the accusations and argue that citizens have legitimate reasons to protest over economic hardship and governance. The public should distinguish political claims from verified findings: no independent investigation or court ruling has established that either party organised violence. Political leaders should condemn attacks regardless of affiliation, while security agencies should investigate impartially and publish evidence where lawful.
electionWatch.imageAlt: Nigeria opposition leaders in the context of the 2027 political debate
electionWatch.imageNote: Contextual image for this report; not represented as a photograph of the specific event unless stated.
electionWatch.whyItMatters: Unproven accusations can inflame tensions and undermine peaceful campaigning.
electionWatch.whatHappensNext: Watch for police findings, evidence presented by the parties and INEC's response to electoral-security concerns.

electionWatch.title: NDC demands forensic audit of alleged ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security costs
electionWatch.summary: The Nigeria Democratic Congress is questioning an ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL receivables figure linked to pipeline and energy security, demanding disclosure and a forensic audit. The figure and its interpretation require examination of audited accounts and government explanations.
electionWatch.content: The NDC has challenged the Tinubu administration over what it describes as an opaque ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security bill or receivables balance associated with NNPCL. The party says the amount is larger than the 2025 defence and security allocation and is demanding a forensic audit, disclosure of contractors and an account of services delivered. This is an opposition party's interpretation of the company's financial disclosures, not proof that ₦11.2 trillion was paid out as a single contract or that funds were misappropriated. The government and NNPCL should publish a clear reconciliation of the accounting entries, contractual obligations, payments, beneficiaries and security outcomes.
electionWatch.imageAlt: President Bola Tinubu, contextual image for scrutiny of government oil-security spending
electionWatch.imageNote: Contextual image for this report; not represented as a photograph of the specific event unless stated.
electionWatch.whyItMatters: Transparent accounting of oil revenue and security expenditure is central to public trust, especially while communities face insecurity.
electionWatch.whatHappensNext: The key test is whether NNPCL and the government publish a detailed, independently auditable explanation and respond to the party's claims.

electionWatch.title: Senate calls for investigation into reported attacks involving Tinubu, Obi and Atiku
electionWatch.summary: The Senate has called for an investigation into reported attacks involving political leaders and warned that candidates found responsible for electoral violence could face sanctions. The motion is not a finding of guilt against any politician.
electionWatch.content: The Senate's intervention follows reports of attacks and disruption involving political convoys and campaign activities. Lawmakers have urged investigations and warned that the Electoral Act provides consequences for electoral violence. The inquiry must establish the facts of each incident and identify individual responsibility; it should not be used to prejudge any party or candidate. Candidates, supporters and journalists must be able to participate in political life without intimidation.
electionWatch.imageNote: Contextual image for this report; not represented as a photograph of the specific event unless stated.
electionWatch.whyItMatters: Safety of political actors and voters is a condition for credible elections.
electionWatch.whatHappensNext: Watch for formal inquiry steps, police findings and any INEC guidance to political parties.

articles.title: APC accuses ADC and NDC of fuelling protests; opposition demands evidence
articles.summary: The APC campaign council has accused opposition parties of sponsoring protests and political disruption. The ADC and NDC reject the claims and say public anger over hardship is genuine. No independent finding proving the allegation has been reported.
articles.content: The exchange has sharpened political tensions ahead of the 2027 elections. The APC Presidential Campaign Council alleges that opposition parties are organising protests and recruiting young people to disrupt political activities. The ADC and NDC deny the accusations and argue that citizens have legitimate reasons to protest over economic hardship and governance. Political leaders should condemn attacks regardless of affiliation, while security agencies should investigate impartially and publish evidence where lawful.

articles.title: NDC demands forensic audit of alleged ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security costs
articles.summary: The Nigeria Democratic Congress is questioning an ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL receivables figure linked to pipeline and energy security, demanding disclosure and a forensic audit. The figure and its interpretation require examination of audited accounts and government explanations.
articles.content: The NDC has challenged the Tinubu administration over what it describes as an opaque ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security bill or receivables balance associated with NNPCL. The party says the amount is larger than the 2025 defence and security allocation and is demanding a forensic audit, disclosure of contractors and an account of services delivered. This is an opposition party's interpretation of the company's financial disclosures, not proof that ₦11.2 trillion was paid out as a single contract or that funds were misappropriated. The government and NNPCL should publish a clear reconciliation of the accounting entries, contractual obligations, payments, beneficiaries and security outcomes.

articles.imageNote: Contextual image for this report; not represented as a photograph of the specific event unless stated.
articles.whyItMatters: Transparent accounting of oil revenue and security expenditure is central to public trust, especially while communities face insecurity.
articles.whatHappensNext: The key test is whether NNPCL and the government publish a detailed, independently auditable explanation and respond to the party's claims.

articles.title: Iran expands Gulf attacks, targeting US base in Kuwait and Bahrain
articles.summary: Iran widened its attacks across the Gulf on Wednesday, targeting a US air base in Kuwait and launching repeated attacks toward Bahrain. Kuwait and Bahrain said their air defences intercepted threats; no immediate casualties or damage were reported.
articles.content: The Associated Press reports that Iran expanded attacks across the Gulf, targeting the US Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and launching further attacks toward Bahrain. articles.title: UK sanctions eight Israeli firms linked to West Bank settlements and aid-blocking group
articles.summary: The UK has imposed asset freezes on eight Israeli construction and property firms involved in West Bank settlement expansion, and on the activist group Tzav 9, which Britain says has blocked aid convoys to Gaza.
articles.content: The British government announced asset freezes targeting eight construction and property development firms it says are involved in illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist group accused of obstructing humanitarian aid entering Gaza. articles.title: France strike: unions maintain pressure over wages as budget talks continue
articles.summary: Public-sector workers have staged nationwide demonstrations over pay and purchasing power. Unions remain dissatisfied with the government's refusal to grant a general pay rise for a fourth consecutive year.
articles.content: France's public-sector strike reflects a wider dispute over wages, purchasing power and the government's 2027 budget. Unions say public employees have lost real income since 2017 and want general pay increases. articles.title: Two trains collide near Prague; 46 people injured
articles.summary: A collision near Prague's main railway station injured 46 people, including four with life-threatening injuries. Passengers were evacuated and investigators are examining the cause.
articles.content: Czech emergency services said two trains collided near Prague's main railway station on Tuesday. Forty-six people were injured, four with life-threatening injuries; others suffered moderate or minor injuries. All passengers were evacuated and taken for medical care. Rail services were suspended while investigators examined the circumstances. Authorities have not yet established the cause, so speculation about driver error or equipment failure should be avoided until the inquiry reports its findings.
articles.imageNote: Contextual image for this report; not represented as a photograph of the specific event unless stated.

articles.title: Myanmar Rohingya case: ICJ ruling expected Thursday in landmark genocide proceedings
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice is expected to issue a substantive ruling on Thursday in The Gambia's case alleging Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention during the 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya.
articles.content: The International Court of Justice is preparing a major decision in a case brought by The Gambia concerning Myanmar's 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya. businessNews.title: NDC demands forensic audit of alleged ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security costs
businessNews.summary: The Nigeria Democratic Congress is questioning an ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL receivables figure linked to pipeline and energy security, demanding disclosure and a forensic audit. The figure and its interpretation require examination of audited accounts and government explanations.
businessNews.content: The NDC has challenged the Tinubu administration over what it describes as an opaque ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security bill or receivables balance associated with NNPCL. The party says the amount is larger than the 2025 defence and security allocation and is demanding a forensic audit, disclosure of contractors and an account of services delivered. This is an opposition party's interpretation of the company's financial disclosures, not proof that ₦11.2 trillion was paid out as a single contract or that funds were misappropriated. The government and NNPCL should publish a clear reconciliation of the accounting entries, contractual obligations, payments, beneficiaries and security outcomes.

businessNews.content: The Associated Press reports that Iran expanded attacks across the Gulf, targeting the US Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and launching further attacks toward Bahrain. Kuwait said its air defences intercepted drones, while Bahrain reported interceptions. The exchanges follow US strikes on Iranian military sites and a naval blockade that is pressuring Iran's economy and oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. AP also reported an attack on an ADNOC tanker in the strait on Tuesday, with one crew member missing and 11 injured. Military claims and damage assessments should be attributed carefully. He highlighted tariff relief with China, expanded access for financial firms and plans to increase liquefied natural gas exports to Asia. editorial.title: Public money must be traceable — and political allegations must be tested
editorial.imageAlt: Nigeria government and political accountability context image
editorial.summary: The NDC's demand for an audit of NNPCL's reported pipeline-security receivables deserves a transparent official response, but the party's claims must not be treated as proven findings.
editorial.content: Nigeria needs clear public accounting of the money associated with protecting oil and gas infrastructure. NNPCL and the government should explain the ₦11.2 trillion figure, identify the accounting basis, disclose relevant contracts where lawful and demonstrate measurable security outcomes. At the same time, political parties must distinguish an audited balance, a contractual obligation, a payment and an allegation of wrongdoing. Transparency and due process are not competing principles; both are essential.

analysis.title: Why the Strait of Hormuz remains a global economic pressure point
analysis.imageAlt: Gulf shipping and maritime security illustration
analysis.summary: The wider Gulf attacks raise risks to commercial vessels, insurance costs, energy markets and import-dependent economies.
analysis.content: The latest reported attacks show that the risk is no longer confined to one location. Even without a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz, threats to ships and infrastructure can increase insurance premiums, freight costs and oil-market volatility. Countries in Asia are especially exposed because of their dependence on imported energy, while consumers in Europe and Africa can feel the effects through fuel and transport costs. Reliable vessel tracking, verified incident reports and diplomatic de-escalation are essential.

analysis.title: Nigeria's ₦11.2 trillion pipeline-security debate needs a public audit trail
analysis.summary: The NDC's allegation raises a legitimate transparency question, but the accounting figure needs a precise explanation before conclusions can be drawn.
analysis.content: The public needs to know whether the NNPCL figure represents receivables, accrued costs, contractual commitments or cash already paid. These categories are not interchangeable. An independent audit should reconcile the amounts, identify counterparties and test whether services were delivered. Until that evidence is published, the party's claim should be reported as an allegation and the government's explanation sought.

factCheck.claim: The NDC has proved that ₦11.2 trillion was stolen from pipeline-security funds.
factCheck.explanation: The NDC has raised questions about a reported NNPCL receivables figure and demanded an audit. The figure's accounting meaning and any wrongdoing have not been established by the party's allegation alone.

factCheck.claim: The Senate inquiry means Tinubu, Obi or Atiku has been found guilty of electoral violence.
factCheck.explanation: A call for investigation is not a finding of guilt. Responsibility must be established through evidence and due process.

factCheck.claim: The Trump-Xi-Putin meeting has already produced an agreement.
factCheck.explanation: The leaders' meeting is expected Thursday. Xi and Putin have held talks and Trump has arrived in Shenzhen, but no trilateral outcome has been announced.

beyondStatement.title: A financial balance is not automatically a cash payment
beyondStatement.summary: The ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL issue needs precise accounting language: receivables, accrued costs, contractual commitments and payments are different things.
beyondStatement.content: The public debate should focus on the audited records, contract terms, actual payments and measurable results. Political allegations warrant scrutiny, but should not be reported as proven misappropriation without evidence.

beyondStatement.title: A summit schedule is not a summit outcome
beyondStatement.summary: The expected Trump-Xi-Putin meeting is scheduled for Thursday; the leaders have not yet announced any trilateral agreement.
beyondStatement.content: Diplomatic reporting should separate confirmed arrivals and bilateral meetings from planned talks and possible agenda items. Outcomes should be reported only after official statements or independently confirmed decisions.

publicInterestFeature.summary: The reported NNPCL receivables figure and the NDC's audit demand raise questions about transparency, contract disclosure and security outcomes.
publicInterestFeature.content: An independent audit should clarify the accounting basis of the ₦11.2 trillion figure, identify the contracts and counterparties involved, explain whether funds were paid or remain receivable, and assess the results achieved. The government should publish a clear response and allow oversight institutions to scrutinise the records.
